  "summary": "An adult couple wants a child and mutually agrees that another adult man may become the biological father. Depending on the generated card, {{user}} may be the husband asking another man to father his wife's child, or the prospective biological father approached by the couple. The arrangement may use direct sexual conception, clinical donation, at-home insemination, repeated fertile-window attempts, or a consensual swinging or non-monogamous context, and the donor's future role ranges from none at all to co-parenting.",
  "core_premise": "An adult couple wants a child and has mutually, knowingly agreed that another adult man may become the biological father — not a hidden affair, not an accidental pregnancy, but an open arrangement negotiated between the three. {{user}} may hold either seat: the partner arranging it, or the man being asked. Conception is the shared goal rather than an accomplished fact. Why a donor is needed, who suggested it, how conception is attempted, what the donor's role becomes, and what the arrangement does to the marriage all vary per card, and every adult's consent, boundaries and future choices remain open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult relationship-drama roleplay opening. Establish the couple and how long they have wanted a child; state plainly why another biological father is wanted or needed; introduce the chosen man and his own life, motives and conditions; and fix which point the opening lands on — the ask, the terms, the night before a first attempt, or the morning after a result. Specify the agreed method, the donor's expected future role, and who else (family, donor's partner, community) is inside or outside the secret. Begin before any irreversible commitment unless the concept explicitly starts mid-arrangement, and never write {{user}}'s answer, presence, consent or feelings in advance.",
  "core_variables": [
    "{{user}}'s perspective: the husband or partner seeking a donor, or the prospective biological father being approached by the couple.",
    "Why another biological father is wanted or needed: infertility, very low fertility, erectile or sexual-function difficulty, genetic concerns, previous sterilisation, treatment effects, failed clinical attempts, or a preference for a known donor.",
    "Who first suggested the arrangement, and how the prospective father was selected.",
    "Conception method: direct sexual conception, clinical donation, at-home insemination, one attempt, repeated fertile-window attempts, or an arrangement continuing until pregnancy occurs.",
    "The donor's expected future role: none at all, acknowledged biology only, family-friend contact, a godfather-style role, or some form of co-parenting.",
    "Whether the couple already practises consensual non-monogamy or swinging, and whether that continues after conception.",
    "The couple's marital health at the start — closeness, grief, blame or avoidance — and how the arrangement tests it.",

    "Secrecy versus openness: what family, friends, community and eventually the child will be told.",
    "Medical, legal and financial practicalities: screening, parentage papers, costs, schedules and records.",
    "How long the couple has already been trying, and how much patience and money remain.",
    "Feelings that grow or blur across repeated attempts, and how boundaries are restated when they wobble.",

    "What happens after a positive test, a failed cycle or a loss, and whether any of it was agreed in advance.",
    "The donor's own life: his reasons for agreeing, his relationships, his goals, his exit conditions.",
    "Which decision the opening scene lands on — the ask itself, the terms, the night before the first attempt, or the morning after a result."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a request succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, cover stories, medical hearsay and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave agreement, refusal, pregnancy, withdrawal, confession, separation and every later player choice open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, fertility agreements, payment and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "The wife must personally and knowingly agree to the reproductive arrangement. Her husband or partner cannot consent on her behalf.",
    "Being asked to become the biological father does not establish {{user}}'s agreement. Begin early enough to preserve his decision unless the generation concept explicitly supplies an existing agreement.",
    "Pregnancy is not guaranteed by one encounter. Repeated attempts may occur, but do not pre-play pregnancy unless the source premise specifically requires an already-successful conception.",
    "Wanting pregnancy and enjoying sex are independent. Enjoyment does not automatically imply leaving the husband; awkwardness does not imply nonconsent.",
    "If swinging is the main engine and conception is incidental, classify primarily under Open Relationship/Crossed Couples rather than this series.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from Bible I I Want Your Baby because this is a knowingly agreed reproductive arrangement involving the existing couple; distinct from You Got Her Pregnant because conception is normally still the goal rather than an accomplished fact.",
    "A diagnosis of infertility is a medical fact about a character, not a verdict on his worth. Do not treat the husband as humiliated or diminished by default.",
    "The donor's fertility, genetics or virility do not make him morally, romantically or sexually superior to the husband.",
    "If the donor has his own partner, her informed consent to his participation must be established or explicitly flagged as unresolved — never silently assumed.",
    "Grief, baby-longing and clinic fatigue are real pressures, but they never license any of the three adults to coerce another.",
    "Keep the child's future interests visible where agreements are made: honesty, stability and parentage clarity can be motives without being mandated outcomes.",
    "Vary the tone: tender, businesslike, awkward, erotic, grief-laden or pragmatic arrangements are all valid; do not default to a single register.",
    "Do not turn repeated attempts into a routinised loop; calendars, moods, failures and ordinary conversation remain part of the fiction.",
    "A donor who changes his mind, a wife who hesitates or a husband who asks to pause are legitimate story turns, not broken premises.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s answer to the ask, his presence at any attempt, or his feelings about a resulting child; all of these remain open.",
    "Medical realism is welcome — screening, ovulation tracking, clinic rules — without turning the premise into a procedure manual.",
    "The couple's marriage is neither doomed nor guaranteed by the arrangement; it may be strengthened, strained or ended by how the three behave.",
    "Keep sexual elements non-graphic at the premise level and open at a playable moment: the ask, the terms, the night before, or the morning after a test."

An adult couple wants a child and has openly, mutually agreed that another adult man may become the biological father; {{user}} is either the husband arranging it or the man being asked. Establish why a donor is needed (infertility, genetics, clinic fatigue or preference for a known father), who the donor is and his own conditions, the conception method (one attempt, fertile windows, clinical or at-home insemination, a swinging context), and his future role from none to co-parenting. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and {{user}}'s choices remain open."
